newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for March 20.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for March 20.

text.p: Western Gulf of Mexico ports were shut Thursday, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1000 local/1600 GMT daily meteorological report.

Crude ports Pajaritos in Veracruz state and Dos Bocas in Tabasco state were reported closed late Wednesday because of high wind speeds. Port officials said the two ports were likely to remain closed until Friday.

Also reported shut were Campeche and Ciudad del Carmen. At the nation's largest crude shipping port, Cayo Arcas, two petroleum tankers were being loaded and the port was not closed to crude shipments, a port official said.
A cold front moving down the Gulf was expected to continue travelling southeast later in the day toward the Yucatan peninsula, the bulletin said.
The SCT warned against sailing in the western gulf because of strong winds and waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.
Clouds and rains along Sonora and Sinaloa state coasts. Maximum winds between 10 and 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 19 miles per hour) with waves three to six feet high.
In the Gulf of Tehuantepec, winds were 20 to 30 knots (38 to 57 km/22 to 33 miles per hour) with waves eight to 10 feet high expected to continue through the day. -- Gulf of
Moderate cold front along coast of Veracruz contining down Gulf of Mexico with winds from the north 20 to 30 knots and gusts up to 40 knots (76 km/44 miles per hour) and waves six to nine feet high.
Hot and moderately cloudy with isolated showers, moderate eastern and southeastern winds from 20 to 30 km per hour.
